annotation_description: Playing Island instead of Steam Vents on turn 1 is slightly suboptimal. With Sleight of Hand in hand (a U sorcery to cast turn 1), the player wants to cast it this turn. Both Island and Steam Vents can produce U, but playing Steam Vents turn 1 (paying 2 life to have it enter untapped) is better because it preserves flexibility for future turns. The hand has no red cards currently, but Steam Vents entering tapped later could be costly when the player needs to hold up Spider-Sense or cast Winternight Stories on curve. Playing the shockland early when life is at 20 and the tempo cost is lowest is generally correct sequencing - you want to take shock damage early when it matters least, and save basic lands for later turns when entering tapped would be more punishing.

Playing Hallowed Fountain tapped on turn 1 when Meticulous Archive could have been played instead. Both enter tapped, but Meticulous Archive provides a surveil 1 trigger when it enters, giving card selection advantage. The player has no 1-mana plays available (Seam Rip costs W but there's no target yet since the opponent has no nonland permanents with MV 2 or less), so entering tapped is fine either way, but Meticulous Archive provides strictly more value by letting them surveil. Hallowed Fountain could be played untapped later when the 2 life payment is worth having mana available immediately.

Played Hallowed Fountain (which can conditionally enter untapped) on turn 1 instead of Meticulous Archive (which always enters tapped but provides surveil 1). Since there's nothing to cast turn 1, the Fountain will enter tapped anyway, wasting the surveil value from Archive and using up the flexible land early.

Playing Island instead of Steam Vents is suboptimal. With Steam Vents, the player could pay 2 life to have it enter untapped, giving access to both blue and red mana. Playing a basic Island means one of the two Steam Vents will need to be played later, potentially when entering tapped would be more costly. More importantly, playing Steam Vents untapped now would give 2 blue sources to cast Opt or Sleight of Hand this turn while keeping Spider-Sense mana up. Playing Island achieves the same immediate mana but wastes a chance to diversify mana colors for future turns (Winternight Stories needs blue, but future red cards could matter). However, the more pressing issue is that playing a basic Island over Steam Vents means the player has slightly less flexible mana going forward - though the difference is small since they have two Steam Vents remaining.

With 2 untapped Islands and no meaningful interaction to hold up (Spider-Sense counters instants/sorceries/triggered abilities, which is narrow), casting Sleight of Hand as a sorcery here would help dig toward lands or key spells. The player has Winternight Stories in hand needing 3 mana, and two Steam Vents that need to be played. Casting Sleight of Hand to smooth draws costs very little since the only 'interaction' available is Spider-Sense which requires returning a tapped creature (none exist) so costs 1U anyway. Opt could also be cast at end of opponent's turn, but Sleight of Hand is sorcery-speed only and this was the time to cast it.

With two untapped Islands and no meaningful interaction to hold up (Spider-Sense only counters instants/sorceries/triggered abilities, and the opponent has shown only lands so far), passing without casting a cantrip wastes mana. Sleight of Hand is a sorcery that can only be cast on their own turn, so this was the last chance to use it this turn cycle. Casting Sleight of Hand here would dig toward lands (they need to hit land drops for Winternight Stories and have two Steam Vents in hand) while still leaving up one blue mana for Opt on the opponent's end step if needed. The reasoning about holding up mana is flawed - Spider-Sense costs 1U so it requires both Islands anyway, and there's nothing else meaningful to do at instant speed besides Opt.

Playing Plains instead of Meticulous Archive or Floodfarm Verge is suboptimal. Meticulous Archive would provide the same W/U mana while giving a free surveil 1 trigger to improve card quality, at the cost of entering tapped (which doesn't matter since Kimi25 has no 2-mana plays they want to cast this turn with both lands - they already have Hallowed Fountain untapped for Seam Rip if needed, but opponent has no nonland permanents to target). Floodfarm Verge would also be reasonable since it enters untapped and produces both colors with Hallowed Fountain (a Plains/Island) already in play. Playing a basic Plains wastes the opportunity to get value from Meticulous Archive's surveil or to preserve flexibility with dual lands.

Playing Steam Vents as the land for the turn means it either enters tapped (losing tempo) or costs 2 life. Since the player has two Islands already and wants to cast blue spells (Opt, Sleight of Hand, Winternight Stories), they don't urgently need red mana yet. More importantly, they should consider casting Sleight of Hand or Opt first before deciding which land to play - cantrips might reveal a better land or change priorities. Playing the land before cantripping is a minor sequencing error. However, since the cantrips cost U and they already have 2 Islands, they could cast a cantrip first and then decide on the land drop based on what they see.

The player should play Steam Vents from hand before casting Winternight Stories. Playing the land first gives access to 4 mana instead of 3, which doesn't change the ability to cast Winternight Stories (costs {2}{U}) but leaves an extra mana open for potential responses. More importantly, proper sequencing is to play lands before casting spells. Additionally, Winternight Stories requires drawing 3 then discarding 2 (unless discarding a creature), and the player's hand has mostly spells they want to keep. With only Sunderflock as a creature to discard, they'll likely need to discard 2 cards. Casting Sleight of Hand or Opt first to filter the hand and potentially find a creature card to discard would have been better sequencing.

message: Discard a creature card instead of discarding two cards?
annotation_description: Discarded two lands (Multiversal Passage and Steam Vents) instead of discarding a single creature card (Sunderflock). With only 3 lands on board and now 0 lands in hand, they risk missing crucial land drops needed to cast Eddymurk Crab (which costs 5 with current graveyard discount). Sunderflock requires an Elemental already in play to be reasonably castable and is largely a dead card without Eddymurk Crab on board first.

Missed a critical land drop on turn 3 with only 2 lands in play and 8 cards in hand including three playable lands. With Floodfarm Verge, they could have had 3 lands (including WU sources) to hold up No More Lies against the opponent's next turn. Missing this land drop severely delays Day of Judgment (needs 4 mana) and leaves them unable to interact with the opponent's plays.

Casting Consult the Star Charts before playing a land drop is a sequencing error. With only 2 lands in play, Consult looks at 2 cards. If they played a land first (Floodfarm Verge, Sunbillow Verge, or Meticulous Archive), they'd have 3 lands and look at 3 cards instead, giving a strictly better selection. Additionally, casting this spell taps out their mana on turn 3 when the opponent has cards in graveyard that could enable cheap threats, and they have No More Lies in hand that they can no longer hold up.

Playing Steam Vents as the land drop is suboptimal because they paid 2 life to have it enter untapped (they're at 18 life, suggesting prior shockland payments). With 3 lands already on board and 4 mana available after this land drop, the key consideration is what they need this turn. They have Sleight of Hand and Opt as cantrips, plus counterspells (Spider-Sense, Spell Snare, No More Lies pattern cards). However, the real issue is that Steam Vents provides red mana which isn't needed - their deck appears to be UW with a splash. They already have a Steam Vents on the battlefield. Playing Steam Vents tapped (saving 2 life) would have been fine since they likely just want to hold up counterspell mana (they have 3 untapped lands already). Actually, looking more carefully - they have 3 lands and are playing a 4th. They could cast Sleight of Hand with existing mana before playing the land to see if they find a better land to play. Casting Sleight of Hand first (using 1 of 3 available mana) would let them see 2 cards and potentially find a different/better land, while still being able to play Steam Vents afterward if nothing better shows up.

Casting Sleight of Hand (a sorcery) during main phase when holding Opt (an instant) is a sequencing error. With the opponent having 3 mana up (including white and blue for No More Lies or other interaction), casting the sorcery-speed spell taps mana during the main phase unnecessarily. Opt should be preferred here because: 1) Opt can be cast at end of opponent's turn, preserving mana for Spell Snare or Spider-Sense during the opponent's turn. 2) Even if you want to cast a cantrip now, Sleight of Hand adds to graveyard instant/sorcery count for Eddymurk Crab cost reduction either way, but keeping instant-speed options open is better. 3) Casting Sleight now uses one of the 4 mana, leaving only 3 up, when keeping all 4 up would allow both Spell Snare and Spider-Sense as responses. The player could cast Opt at end of opponent's turn instead and keep more mana open this turn.

With 4 instants/sorceries in the graveyard (Sleight of Hand x2, Winternight Stories, plus the current Sleight resolving), Eddymurk Crab already costs around 3-4 mana. The player has Steam Vents x2 + Island x2 (4 lands) and already holds Eddymurk Crab. Burst Lightning is a versatile removal/burn spell that would be immediately castable and helps deal with early threats from the opponent's white-blue deck, while also adding to the graveyard count for Eddymurk Crab. Glacial Dragonhunt is a 2-mana sorcery that requires discarding to get the damage effect. While Dragonhunt does have value as card filtering and potential removal, Burst Lightning is more efficient instant-speed removal that can be cast alongside other spells. However, Glacial Dragonhunt does have the harmonize ability for graveyard recursion and the discard synergy with Winternight Stories already in the graveyard. This is close but Burst Lightning's flexibility as instant-speed removal seems slightly better given the opponent could deploy threats.

Casting Glacial Dragonhunt as a sorcery with no opposing creatures wastes the damage mode entirely (the 3 damage to a creature has no valid target). Additionally, it taps down to only 1 blue mana, leaving only Spell Snare as protection while the opponent could cast something that Spider-Sense (1U) could counter. Opt would provide card selection while keeping both Spell Snare AND Spider-Sense available.

Glacial Dragonhunt is a 2-mana sorcery on the stack. Kimi25 has No More Lies (W/U) available with exactly the mana to cast it (Hallowed Fountain, Plains, Floodfarm Verge provide W and U). Letting Glacial Dragonhunt resolve allows the opponent to draw a card and potentially deal 3 damage to a creature (though Kimi25 has no creatures, the card draw alone is significant). More importantly, each instant/sorcery in the opponent's graveyard reduces the cost of Eddymurk Crab. The opponent already has 5 cards in their graveyard including instants and sorceries. Letting this resolve adds another spell to the graveyard, making future Eddymurk Crabs cheaper. No More Lies would counter it and exile it (preventing graveyard synergies), and the opponent would need to pay 3 mana they likely don't have available. While countering a card-draw spell with a counterspell is a reasonable use of resources, the decision to let it resolve gives the opponent card advantage and fuels their graveyard strategy for free.

Seam Rip can target any nonland permanent an opponent controls with mana value 2 or less, not just creatures. However, looking at Sonnet Vorthos's battlefield, they only have lands (Islands and Steam Vents), so there are actually no valid nonland permanent targets. Get Lost also has no valid targets since the opponent has no creatures, enchantments, or planeswalkers. The reasoning about 'no targets' is actually correct for the current board state. However, the player should have played Meticulous Archive from hand as their land drop this turn to advance to 5 lands, enabling future plays like Day of Judgment or kicked Consult the Star Charts. The player had Meticulous Archive in hand and passing without playing a land is a missed land drop.

Kimi25 has Seam Rip available for W, which can exile a nonland permanent with mana value 2 or less from the opponent. While the opponent currently has no nonland permanents on the battlefield, Kimi25 also has Meticulous Archive (a tapped land) in hand and could have played it this turn to develop their mana. More importantly, they have 2 untapped lands (Plains and Sunbillow Verge) and chose to pass without playing their land drop (Meticulous Archive). Missing a land drop when holding 6 cards including a 4-mana Day of Judgment they want to cast next turn is a real cost - they need 4 lands untapped to cast Day of Judgment, and playing the Archive now would give them 6 lands next turn instead of 5.

Playing Meticulous Archive (enters tapped) instead of Sunbillow Verge as the land drop. With 4 lands already on board (Hallowed Fountain, Plains, Floodfarm Verge, Sunbillow Verge), Sunbillow Verge would enter and can tap for W (since Plains is controlled) or R. Playing Sunbillow Verge untapped would leave 5 mana available, enough to cast Day of Judgment (2WW) with mana open. Playing Meticulous Archive tapped means only 4 mana available. While the surveil 1 from Archive has some value, the tempo loss of an enters-tapped land is notable. Additionally, the player could have played Sunbillow Verge and then cast Consult the Star Charts or held up No More Lies with 5 lands untapped. The surveil 1 is a minor upside but the tempo difference matters, especially when holding Day of Judgment and counter magic.

Kimi25 has Sunbillow Verge in hand and hasn't played a land this turn. They should play the land first before casting Consult the Star Charts, since Consult looks at the top X cards where X is the number of lands they control. Playing the land first would mean looking at 6 cards instead of 5, giving better card selection. Additionally, having more mana available after resolving the spell could be relevant for holding up interaction.

Chose Hallowed Fountain from Consult the Star Charts when Jeskai Revelation was available. Kimi25 already had Sunbillow Verge in hand for their next land drop, making the extra land redundant. Jeskai Revelation is a powerful finisher that could be cast as early as next turn with 7 mana, and the hand was full of reactive spells but lacked a proactive win condition.

Consult the Star Charts is on the stack with mana value 2, and Spell Snare counters spells with mana value 2. The opponent has 6 lands and is casting a card-selection spell that will let them look at 6 cards and find their best card. Letting this resolve gives the opponent significant card quality advantage. Additionally, Into the Flood Maw is in the graveyard, so Eddymurk Crab costs {4}{U}{U} - still expensive but approaching castable range. Countering the card selection spell would be a clean use of Spell Snare.

Rest in Peace could have been cast here to proactively exile graveyards and prevent future graveyard synergies. The opponent has Into the Flood Maw in their graveyard, and importantly, the opponent appears to be playing a blue deck that likely runs Eddymurk Crab (which costs less for each instant/sorcery in graveyard). Casting Rest in Peace now would be a proactive enchantment that provides ongoing value by exiling all future cards that would go to graveyards, making Eddymurk Crab much more expensive. Additionally, the opponent has 5 mana open including only blue sources, so countermagic is a concern - but passing with no development at all is also questionable when there's a proactive enchantment available.

Used the more flexible counterspell (Spider-Sense) when the narrow one (Spell Snare) would have worked perfectly. Spell Snare costs only {U} vs Spider-Sense's {1}{U}, saving 1 mana this turn. More importantly, Spider-Sense is a broader answer that hits any instant, sorcery, or triggered ability, while Spell Snare only hits MV 2 spells. Using the narrow answer when applicable preserves the flexible one for future threats. The player's reasoning was also incorrect - they claimed Spider-Sense draws a card, which it does not.

message: Select an instant spell, sorcery spell, or triggered ability
annotation_description: Spider-Sense reads 'Counter target instant spell, sorcery spell, or triggered ability.' It is a counterspell, not a copy effect. The player's reasoning ('Spider-Sense copies a spell!') is completely wrong about what the card does. By targeting their own Glacial Dragonhunt with Spider-Sense, they are countering their own spell, losing both cards for nothing. This wastes two cards and the mana spent casting both spells.

Casting Day of Judgment when the opponent has zero creatures on the battlefield. This only destroys Kimi25's own 1/1 Fish Token, wasting a powerful board wipe for no benefit while spending 4 mana on their main phase.

Casting Consult the Star Charts during main phase when the opponent is tapped out wastes the opportunity to hold up countermagic (No More Lies) or removal (Get Lost) during the opponent's turn. With all of the opponent's lands tapped, this was a safe window, but Consult the Star Charts is an instant and could be cast at end of opponent's turn instead, preserving flexibility. More importantly, playing Hallowed Fountain first (from hand) before casting Consult would give 8 lands instead of 7, letting them look at one additional card. Additionally, Rest in Peace could be a strong proactive play here since the opponent has Spider-Sense, Glacial Dragonhunt, and Into the Flood Maw in their graveyard - Glacial Dragonhunt has Harmonize (castable from graveyard) and denying graveyard resources while the opponent is tapped out is valuable.

Chose Tishana's Tidebinder over Restless Anchorage from Consult the Star Charts. The hand is already loaded with reactive spells (No More Lies, Get Lost, Seam Rip, Day of Judgment) and has Hallowed Fountain as a land drop. A UW control deck desperately needs win conditions, and Restless Anchorage is a premium creature-land that serves as an uncounterable threat while also providing mana.

Kimi25 has 5 untapped lands (Plains, Sunbillow Verge, Sunbillow Verge, Fish Token doesn't tap for mana, Meticulous Archive) and the opponent is tapped out with all 5 lands tapped. This is the perfect window to deploy Rest in Peace, which exiles the opponent's graveyard (containing Into the Flood Maw, Glacial Dragonhunt, Spider-Sense) and shuts off graveyard synergies like Harmonize on Glacial Dragonhunt and cost reduction for Eddymurk Crab. With the opponent tapped out, there's zero risk of counterplay. Seam Rip could also be deployed for free targeting nothing relevant, but Rest in Peace is the high-value play here. Additionally, playing Hallowed Fountain from hand (even tapped) would ensure the land drop isn't missed.

Opponent is completely tapped out with no board presence, and has 3 instants/sorceries in graveyard enabling Glacial Dragonhunt harmonize and potential Eddymurk Crab cost reduction. Rest in Peace would resolve for free and shut down these synergies. This is the ideal window to deploy it uncountered.

Rest in Peace would exile the opponent's graveyard (Into the Flood Maw, Glacial Dragonhunt, Spider-Sense) and prevent future graveyard accumulation. The opponent appears to be playing a blue-red spells deck that likely runs Eddymurk Crab or similar cards that benefit from instants/sorceries in the graveyard. Additionally, Glacial Dragonhunt has Harmonize (castable from graveyard), so exiling it now prevents future value. With 3 untapped lands (Plains-producing Sunbillow Verge x2 + Meticulous Archive), Kimi25 could cast Rest in Peace for {1}{W} and still hold up mana for future plays. The opponent is tapped out, so there's no risk of countermagic.

Eddymurk Crab is a 5/5 that costs {5}{U}{U} but gets {1} cheaper for each instant/sorcery in the graveyard. Sonnet Vorthos has 3 instants/sorceries in graveyard (Into the Flood Maw, Glacial Dragonhunt, Spider-Sense), so it costs {2}{U}{U} - very efficiently costed for a 5/5 that also taps up to two creatures on entry. This is a major threat that Kimi25 had multiple answers for. No More Lies would counter it unless opponent pays {3} (they have 5 lands but may not have 3 extra mana after casting the Crab for 4 mana - they'd have exactly 1 mana left, so they cannot pay {3}). Tishana's Tidebinder could counter the ETB trigger but still leaves a 5/5 on board. Get Lost could destroy it but gives two Map tokens. No More Lies was clearly the best option here - it would cleanly counter the Crab since the opponent tapped 4 of their 5 lands to cast it and cannot pay {3}. Instead, Kimi25 let a 5/5 resolve that will also tap two of their permanents.

Kimi25 has a 5/5 Eddymurk Crab on the opponent's board threatening significant damage, and the opponent is at 14 life with all lands tapped. Kimi25 has Get Lost available (costs {1}{W}) which can destroy the Eddymurk Crab right now while the opponent has no mana to respond. Instead, they passed, allowing the Crab to remain on board. They also have Day of Judgment available for 4 mana (they have access to enough mana with their untapped lands). The opponent's lands are all tapped, meaning they cannot counter or interact. This is a prime window to remove the threat.

Kimi25 has a 5/5 Eddymurk Crab threatening them on the opponent's board. Get Lost cleanly destroys it for 2 mana, while Tishana's Tidebinder is a 3/2 flash creature that doesn't address the Crab at all (its ETB counters activated/triggered abilities, not creatures). The opponent has 4 tapped lands and only Riverpyre Verge untapped, so they likely can't protect the Crab. Deploying Tidebinder leaves the 5/5 Crab on board to attack next turn for a quarter of Kimi25's life total, while Get Lost would remove it immediately. The Map tokens given to the opponent are a minor downside compared to taking repeated 5/5 hits.

Kimi25 chose to cast Tishana's Tidebinder over Get Lost to deal with the opponent's Eddymurk Crab. Tidebinder is a 3/2 that counters activated/triggered abilities, but the Crab's ETB has already resolved. Tidebinder doesn't remove the 5/5 Crab - it just puts a 3/2 body on board that can't profitably block it. Get Lost would actually destroy the Crab, which is the main threat. However, Tidebinder does add a body to the board and preserves Get Lost for later, and Kimi25 also has Day of Judgment as a backup plan. The Crab represents a significant clock (5 damage per turn), so removing it now with Get Lost might be more urgent. That said, playing Tidebinder develops the board and keeps removal options open, so this is debatable.

Kimi25 has a 5/5 Eddymurk Crab on the opponent's board that needs to be dealt with, and the opponent is tapped out. Kimi25 has Get Lost which destroys it at instant speed, or Day of Judgment which wipes the board (losing only a 1/1 Fish token and Tishana's Tidebinder). Casting Stock Up here is a card draw spell when there's an urgent threat on board. More importantly, casting Stock Up uses 3 mana, which means Kimi25 can no longer cast Day of Judgment (costs 2WW = 4 mana) this turn. With 7 lands, they could have cast Day of Judgment and still had mana left, or cast Get Lost to remove the Crab while the opponent is tapped out. The opponent has Spider-Sense and Into the Flood Maw in graveyard (not castable), and all lands tapped, so this was the perfect window to remove the 5/5 threat. Stock Up draws cards but doesn't address the board problem, and the opponent will untap next turn with the 5/5 and open mana for countermagic.

Kimi25 has Stock Up on the stack (opponent's spell resolving) and has No More Lies available with mana to cast it. Stock Up is a card advantage spell that would let the opponent draw 2 cards from the top 5. Countering it with No More Lies would deny significant card advantage and exile the spell. The opponent (Sonnet Vorthos) has all lands tapped, meaning they can't pay the {3} for No More Lies. Additionally, Kimi25 has Tishana's Tidebinder on the battlefield and the opponent has an Eddymurk Crab as a serious threat. Letting the opponent refuel with 2 cards when they're tapped out and you have a free counter opportunity is a meaningful mistake.

message: Select a card ORDER to put on the BOTTOM of your library (last one chosen will be bottommost)
annotation_description: Kimi25 has a 5/5 Eddymurk Crab on the opponent's side that is a major threat. They have Get Lost in hand which cleanly answers it, and they also have Day of Judgment available. The opponent is tapped out (all lands tapped), so there's no risk of countermagic. Passing without dealing with the Crab means they'll take 5 damage on the opponent's next attack, and the opponent will untap and have mana to protect it. The reasoning that 'I have TWO creatures' ignores that a Fish token (1/1) and Tishana's Tidebinder (3/2) are far less threatening than a 5/5, and the Crab will dominate combat. Additionally, Stock Up is on the stack resolving for Kimi25, so they should use the card advantage moment to stabilize the board.

Declined to cast Get Lost on Eddymurk Crab (5/5) while the opponent was completely tapped out with no mana for counterplay. The Crab can block and kill Tishana's Tidebinder (3/2), and removing it would push through 4 damage instead of likely just 1 from the Fish token. While Kimi25 has Day of Judgment as a backup plan, using Get Lost here when the opponent can't interact is efficient and removes a major threat while pushing damage.

Casting Sunderflock before Opt is slightly suboptimal sequencing. Casting Opt first (and potentially finding something better or more information) before committing to Sunderflock would be better, especially since there's plenty of mana for both plus holding up Spell Snare. Additionally, deploying both major threats simultaneously exposes them to a single Day of Judgment, though Spell Snare can't counter it anyway (MV 4).

Kimi25 allowed Sunderflock (a 5/5 flyer that bounces all non-Elemental creatures) to resolve when they had No More Lies available with the mana to cast it. Sunderflock's ETB trigger will return the Fish token to hand (though that's minor). More critically, a 5/5 flyer is an enormous threat that will close the game quickly. Kimi25 has Day of Judgment in hand which could answer it, but spending a board wipe on a single creature is very inefficient, and the opponent likely has countermagic (they play blue). No More Lies would have countered Sunderflock unless the opponent paid 3 additional mana. Looking at the board, the opponent cast Sunderflock with Eddymurk Crab already on board (reducing its cost), and likely tapped most/all their lands, making it very difficult to pay the additional 3. This was a must-counter threat - a 5/5 flyer that also bounces non-Elementals.

Kimi25 declined to cast Get Lost on either Eddymurk Crab (5/5) or Sunderflock (5/5 flyer) while having the mana to do so. The opponent has 10 power on board including a 5/5 flyer, representing a fast clock. While Kimi25 has Day of Judgment in hand, they only have 4 untapped lands (Plains, Sunbillow Verge, Meticulous Archive, Hallowed Fountain) and Day of Judgment costs 2WW - they can cast it next turn. However, Get Lost at instant speed could remove Sunderflock (the flying threat that's harder to block) right now, and Day of Judgment could clean up next turn if needed. The reasoning about 'not revealing their hand' makes no sense when facing 10 power of threats. More critically, Sunderflock's ETB trigger is about to bounce the Fish token (a minor loss), but the real issue is leaving two massive threats on board when you could efficiently answer one now. Not using Get Lost on the Sunderflock (which flies over blockers and is the more dangerous threat) is a meaningful missed opportunity.

With a Sunderflock (MV 9 Elemental) already on the battlefield, the second Sunderflock in hand costs 0 mana due to the cost reduction. Instead of deploying a free 5/5 flyer (which would give 20 flying power for lethal next turn against the opponent's 18 life), the player cast Opt for minor card selection. The free Sunderflock would also bounce no relevant creatures since the opponent has none and Eddymurk Crab is an Elemental.

Kimi25 has Day of Judgment in hand and reasons they should wait to board wipe, but the opponent has an Eddymurk Crab (5/5) AND a Sunderflock (5/5 flying) already on the battlefield. The opponent is casting Opt, not a creature - the creatures are already deployed. Meanwhile, Kimi25 is at 18 life facing 10 power of attackers (5 of which has flying). The correct play here is to use No More Lies or Spell Snare (not in hand) to counter the Opt - actually, countering Opt with No More Lies is wasteful. The real issue is that Kimi25 should be casting Day of Judgment THIS turn during their main phase rather than passing. However, the decision point is specifically about whether to counter an Opt on the stack. Countering Opt with No More Lies (spending 2 mana to counter a cantrip that costs 1) is reasonable value denial, preventing the opponent from finding answers to Day of Judgment. But declining is also defensible since they want mana open. The reasoning mentions Sunderflock as a '3/2 flyer' when it's actually a 5/5 flyer - the villain is confusing it with Tishana's Tidebinder. This misread of the board could lead to underestimating the threat level, though the decision to not counter Opt is not terrible in isolation.

Declined to cast a second Sunderflock for just {U}{U} (discounted by the first Sunderflock's MV 9). This would add another 5/5 flyer to the board, increasing the clock from 2 turns to potentially 1-2 turns. Both existing creatures are Elementals so they wouldn't be bounced. The risk of overextending into a board wipe is minimal since they're already committed with two large threats.

Kimi25 has two Get Lost in hand and is about to take 5 damage from an unblocked Eddymurk Crab (going from 18 to 13 life), with a Sunderflock also on board threatening 5 flying damage next turn. They have untapped mana available (Plains, Sunbillow Verge, Hallowed Fountain = at least WW available) to cast Get Lost on the Eddymurk Crab before damage. Additionally, they have Day of Judgment in hand which could clean up both creatures next turn, but letting both creatures survive means taking potentially 10 damage next turn (5 ground + 5 flying), putting them to 3 life - extremely dangerous. Removing the Crab now prevents 5 damage and buys time to Day of Judgment the Sunderflock next turn.

Kimi25 had two copies of Get Lost in hand and the mana to cast one, facing a Sunderflock (5/5 flyer) and an Eddymurk Crab attacking. The Sunderflock is a massive threat that will continue dealing 5 damage per turn through the air. By not casting Get Lost on either attacker (particularly the Sunderflock), Kimi25 took 5 damage from the Eddymurk Crab unnecessarily. The reasoning about 'waiting to see their minions' makes no sense - attackers are already declared in the combat phase, and Get Lost can be cast as an instant to destroy an attacker before damage. The Sunderflock in particular is the primary threat that should be removed, as it's a 5/5 flyer that also bounced all non-Elemental creatures when it entered.

Kimi25 declined to cast Get Lost on the Sunderflock (5/5 flyer) during combat. While they have Day of Judgment in hand for their next main phase, using Get Lost now would prevent 5 damage and save them from going to 8 life (or lower). Day of Judgment costs 4 mana and they have 7 lands but some are tapped - they need to verify they can cast it next turn. The risk is that if they don't draw into the right mana or if the opponent has countermagic for Day of Judgment, they've taken unnecessary damage. However, Get Lost gives the opponent two Map tokens which provide card selection, and if Day of Judgment resolves next turn it handles both creatures at once without giving away Map tokens. The line is defensible but taking 5+ extra damage at 13 life when you could remove the biggest threat is risky, especially since the opponent has open mana for potential counterspells on the Day of Judgment.

Sunderflock is a 5/5 flyer that represents a fast clock and is the opponent's primary win condition. Kimi25 has Get Lost available at instant speed for just {1}{W} with 4 untapped lands (Plains, Sunbillow Verge, Hallowed Fountain, Meticulous Archive). While Day of Judgment is in hand, it costs {2}{W}{W} and won't be castable until next turn at the earliest. Meanwhile, Sunderflock will attack for 5 in the air next turn, bringing Kimi25 from 13 to 8 life. Using Get Lost now removes the threat immediately while the opponent has most lands tapped (only Steam Vents, Riverpyre Verge, and Island untapped - 3 mana for potential countermagic). The opponent does have Spider-Sense in the graveyard but not in hand. Waiting gives the opponent time to develop more threats or hold up more countermagic. The map tokens from Get Lost are relatively minor compared to letting a 5/5 flyer continue attacking.

Sonnet Vorthos cast Glacial Dragonhunt, which draws a card and then may discard to deal 3 damage to a creature. Kimi25 Villain has Sunderflock (5/5 flyer) on the opponent's board as a major threat, and the opponent's lands are all tapped. Kimi25 Villain could have cast Get Lost targeting Sunderflock in response to Glacial Dragonhunt. With the opponent tapped out, this was a clean opportunity to destroy the 5/5 flyer without fear of countermagic. Instead, Kimi25 Villain passed, letting the turn cycle end and giving the opponent a chance to untap and protect Sunderflock with counterspells on future turns.

Failed to play Island from hand before casting Day of Judgment. Should always make land drop before casting spells when there's no strategic reason to hold the land. This costs nothing and provides an additional mana source for future turns (8 lands instead of 7).

Spirebluff Canal enters tapped because Sonnet Vorthos already controls 6 other lands (well over the 2 threshold). Riverpyre Verge would have entered untapped and immediately produced U or R, giving access to 7 mana this turn instead of 6. The reasoning incorrectly stated Spirebluff Canal comes in untapped.

The opponent's graveyard contains Eddymurk Crab and Sunderflock plus 3 instants/sorceries that discount future Eddymurk Crabs. Rest in Peace would exile all of this for just 2 mana, and with 8 lands available, Kimi25 could still hold up No More Lies (WU) afterwards. The graveyard is actively enabling the opponent's cost-reduction strategy.

Kimi25 declined to cast Rest in Peace despite having 8 lands and No More Lies available for backup. The opponent has Eddymurk Crab and Sunderflock in graveyard plus 3 instants/sorceries that enable cost reduction. Casting Rest in Peace (2 mana) while holding No More Lies (2 mana) would exile all graveyards on entry and prevent future graveyard-based cost reduction, with counter protection available.

Kimi25 has Rest in Peace in hand and the mana to cast it. The opponent has 5 cards in their graveyard including Eddymurk Crab and Sunderflock, which are key threats that cost less with graveyard-fueled mechanics (Eddymurk Crab costs {1} less for each instant/sorcery in graveyard). Rest in Peace would exile all graveyards and prevent future graveyard accumulation, making the opponent's Eddymurk Crabs and Sunderflock much more expensive to cast. Additionally, Kimi25 has 8 lands and only used some for earlier plays, so there's mana available. While Kimi25's own graveyard has 6 cards, none of them appear to matter for future gameplay. Casting Rest in Peace here is pure upside - it's an enchantment that taxes the opponent's future threats significantly.

Rest in Peace would exile all graveyards, which is highly relevant here. The opponent has Eddymurk Crab and Sunderflock in their graveyard along with several instants/sorceries. While those cards are already in the graveyard, Rest in Peace's ongoing effect would prevent future cards from entering the graveyard, which matters because the opponent's strategy revolves around cost reduction from graveyard cards (Eddymurk Crab costs less for each instant/sorcery in graveyard). Additionally, casting Rest in Peace now when the opponent is fully tapped out means it resolves for free with no risk of countermagic. The opponent has 5 cards in graveyard including instants and sorceries that could enable future cost-reduced threats. Passing here wastes a window where the opponent can't interact.

Seam Rip has no valid target - the opponent controls zero nonland permanents. The ETB trigger will fizzle and the card is completely wasted. Meanwhile, Rest in Peace would exile the opponent's graveyard (containing Eddymurk Crab, Sunderflock, 2x Opt, Spider-Sense, Into the Flood Maw) which is highly relevant since Eddymurk Crab's cost reduction depends on instants/sorceries in graveyard.

Rest in Peace costs {1}{W} (mana value 2), making it a legal target for Spell Snare. Allowing it to resolve exiles the entire graveyard, which is devastating for Sonnet Vorthos's strategy - they have 6 cards in graveyard including Eddymurk Crab and Sunderflock, and Rest in Peace's static ability means all future cards that would go to the graveyard are exiled instead. This shuts off graveyard synergies (like cost reduction for Eddymurk Crab) and is a permanent enchantment that's difficult to remove in blue. Sonnet Vorthos has TWO copies of Spell Snare in hand, which perfectly counters this 2-mana spell, and has plenty of mana available.

Seam Rip exiles a nonland permanent an opponent controls with mana value 2 or less, but the opponent has NO nonland permanents on the battlefield - only lands. Seam Rip has no valid target and this cast accomplishes nothing, wasting a card. The opponent's board is entirely lands (Island, Island, Steam Vents, Steam Vents, Riverpyre Verge, Island, Spirebluff Canal, Island).

In a control mirror with no threats on board, Sonnet Vorthos already had 3 Spell Snares, Spider-Sense, and Bounce Off - a hand full of reactive spells with zero threats or card advantage. Spell Pierce is weak when the opponent has 8 lands and can easily pay {2}. Abandon Attachments would allow converting redundant Spell Snares into fresh cards, helping find win conditions in a game where neither player has threats.

Kimi25 declined to play Cori Mountain Monastery, missing a land drop. They have 8 lands in play and a land in hand. Playing the monastery would give them 9 mana sources, allowing them to potentially activate its exile-and-play ability ({3}{R}, {T}) in future turns as a mana sink. The board is empty of creatures on both sides, so there's no downside to playing it. Missing a land drop when you have a land in hand is almost never correct, especially when the land has a useful activated ability that can generate card advantage.

Kimi25 incorrectly believed they had no red mana sources, but Sunbillow Verge can produce {R} when you control a Plains (which they do via Plains and Hallowed Fountain). They could have activated Cori Mountain Monastery's {3}{R},{T} ability to exile the top card of their library for potential card advantage, which is a free mana sink with no downside when they have nothing else productive to do.

Kimi25 passed without activating Cori Mountain Monastery, wasting an opportunity for free card advantage. With 8 lands and no opponent threats on board, activating the Monastery ({3}{R}, {T}) would still leave mana open for No More Lies or other interaction, while generating an extra card to play.

Declined to activate Cori Mountain Monastery's ability as a mana sink when there was nothing else productive to do with mana. The activation exiles the top card and lets you play it, generating card advantage. Activated abilities can't be countered by the opponent's likely counterspells (Spell Pierce, No More Lies, etc.).

Casting Jeskai Revelation (an instant) during main phase instead of at end of opponent's turn. This taps out Kimi25 during their own turn, leaving no mana for countermagic (No More Lies in hand) during the opponent's turn. The opponent has 8 blue lands untapped and likely has countermagic or threats. Casting at end of opponent's turn would allow holding up No More Lies during their turn and still get the same value from Jeskai Revelation.

With 8 lands on the battlefield and no creatures from either player on board, the Villain declined to activate Cori Mountain Monastery's ability ({3}{R}, {T}: Exile the top card of your library. Until the end of your next turn, you may play that card). This is a pure card advantage ability that could be activated at the end of the opponent's turn, but since this is postcombat main phase with mana available and nothing else productive to do, activating it now is reasonable too. The opponent has no board presence, so there's no immediate need to hold up mana for removal spells. While the hand is already strong, declining a free card advantage activation when you have spare mana is leaving value on the table. The Villain could activate the Monastery and still hold up mana for No More Lies (WU) with the remaining untapped lands.

Failed to cast Jeskai Revelation when opponent has an empty board and 8 untapped lands. Jeskai Revelation would bounce an opponent's land, deal 4 damage (opponent goes to 9), create two 1/1 prowess monks, draw 2 cards, and gain 4 life (going to 17). This is enormous value that shouldn't be held indefinitely. While casting at opponent's end step would be slightly better, completely passing the turn without deploying this is a significant waste of tempo.

Kimi25 has Cori Mountain Monastery available to activate at end of opponent's turn ({3}{R}, {T}: Exile the top card of your library. Until the end of your next turn, you may play that card). With 8 lands untapped and nothing else to do, this is a free card advantage activation that costs nothing meaningful. The exiled card can be played until end of next turn, so there's no downside to activating it during the opponent's combat/end step. Passing without using this mana sink wastes potential card advantage.

Kimi25 has Cori Mountain Monastery available to activate at end of turn as a mana sink, exiling the top card of their library for potential extra value. With 8 lands including the Monastery, they have the mana to activate it ({3}{R}, {T}). In a stalled board state where both players are at 13 life with empty boards, generating card advantage through the Monastery activation is pure upside - they get to see an extra card and potentially play it until end of next turn. There's no reason to hold back on this activation, especially at end of turn when the mana would go unused anyway.

Declined to activate Cori Mountain Monastery's card advantage ability ({3}{R}, {T}) during combat when they had excess mana and no other pressing uses. With 8+ lands and the opponent having an empty board, they could activate the Monastery to exile the top card for potential future play while still holding up No More Lies ({W}{U}) with remaining mana.

Kimi25 passed with 8 lands untapped without activating Cori Mountain Monastery's impulse draw ability. They could activate it for {3}{R} and still hold up No More Lies ({W}{U}) with remaining mana. In a control mirror at parity, failing to use a mana sink that generates card advantage is leaving value on the table.

With the opponent at 13 life and two Burst Lightnings in hand (4 damage total, or 8 if kicked), the player declined to fire off Burst Lightnings at the opponent's face during their postcombat main phase. With 8 lands available, they could cast both Burst Lightnings (2 damage each = 4 total) while still holding up countermagic. However, this is a control mirror where the player has no board presence and the opponent has 13 life, so 4 damage doesn't threaten lethal soon. Holding burn for potential creatures or saving mana for counterspells is defensible, but using at least one Burst Lightning end-of-opponent's-turn would be strictly better than doing nothing on your own turn, since it preserves the option to counter spells. Casting them on your own main phase is suboptimal timing regardless.

Kimi25 has 8 lands including sources that can produce all colors, and it's the opponent's end step (post-combat main on their own turn, but opponent has no creatures on board). Cori Mountain Monastery's activated ability ({3}{R}, {T}: Exile the top card of your library. Until the end of your next turn, you may play that card) is available as a mana sink. With 8 lands and nothing else productive to do, activating this ability would generate card advantage at no real cost - the mana would otherwise go unused. This is a pure-upside activated ability being declined.

Spider-Sense is arguably more valuable than the third Spell Snare. Spider-Sense counters instants, sorceries, and triggered abilities, giving it broader coverage than Spell Snare which only hits MV 2 spells. Having three Spell Snares is redundant - they're narrow and situational, only useful against exactly 2-mana spells. Spider-Sense can also be cast for just U with its web-slinging cost if a creature is available, and it hits things Spell Snare cannot (like Day of Judgment, Jeskai Revelation, or triggered abilities).

With 8 lands available and the opponent tapped out (or at least with an empty board), Kimi25 could have activated Cori Mountain Monastery's ability ({3}{R}, {T}: Exile the top card of your library. Until the end of your next turn, you may play that card) to generate card advantage. This is a pure-upside mana sink that costs nothing meaningful since the mana would otherwise go unused. The opponent has no creatures on board, so Day of Judgment and Get Lost have no targets anyway - but using the Monastery activation would at least give an extra card option. Passing with 8 untapped lands and a mana sink available wastes potential value.

Cast Abandon Attachments (an instant) during their own main phase instead of waiting until the opponent's end step. While they still have 6 mana remaining for counterspells, casting it at end of opponent's turn would preserve maximum flexibility and give more information about what the opponent does. Additionally, with 8 cards in hand, casting this (discard 1, draw 2) puts them at 9 cards, meaning they'll need to discard 2 at end of turn - they should have waited for opponent's end step to maximize information before making discard decisions.

Abandon Attachments (mana value 2) is on the stack, likely cast by the opponent to draw 2 cards. Sonnet Vorthos has three Spell Snares in hand, which perfectly counter mana value 2 spells. Letting the opponent resolve a card-draw spell for free when holding the exact answer is a significant mistake that gives the opponent unnecessary card advantage.

Abandon Attachments is on the stack (a 2-mana value spell) and Kimi25 has Spell Snare in hand, which perfectly counters spells with mana value 2. Abandon Attachments lets the opponent discard a card to draw two, generating significant card advantage. Letting it resolve gives the opponent a 2-for-1 card draw spell for free. Spell Snare costs only 1 mana and would cleanly counter it.

Declined to activate Cori Mountain Monastery's ability to exile the top card of library for potential card advantage, despite having 8 lands and being able to still hold up countermagic (No More Lies or Spell Snare) with the remaining 3 untapped lands. The opponent has an empty board, making this essentially risk-free card advantage.

Casting Burst Lightning during combat on an empty board with no attackers seems premature. The opponent is at 13 life, so two Burst Lightnings only deal 4 damage total (non-kicked). There's no reason to fire off burn spells now rather than holding them. Burst Lightning could be cast at end of opponent's turn to preserve the option of using mana for counterspells (Spell Snare, Spell Pierce) during the opponent's turn. Casting it during your own combat phase when you have no creatures attacking means you're tapping mana that could be held up for interaction on the opponent's turn.

Cast Burst Lightning unkicked for 2 damage to face when they could easily kick it next turn (9 lands available) for 4 damage. Also loses flexibility of using it as creature removal. With 3 Spell Snares and Spell Pierce in hand, there's no urgency to spend this card now for half value.

Jeskai Revelation is a 7-mana spell on the stack that will deal 4 damage, bounce a permanent, create two tokens, draw two cards, and gain 4 life. This is a massive swing spell that should be the target of the bounce effect itself. By choosing to bounce an opponent's Steam Vents (an untapped land), Kimi25 is allowing Jeskai Revelation to fully resolve - the opponent gets all the benefits (4 damage, 2 tokens, 2 cards, 4 life gain) while only losing a land temporarily. Bouncing the Jeskai Revelation spell itself would counter it entirely (returning it to the opponent's hand without any of its effects resolving), which is enormously better. Alternatively, Kimi25 has countermagic in hand (No More Lies, Spell Snare) but those can't counter a 7-mana spell effectively. Wait - actually, Kimi25 is the one being targeted by Jeskai Revelation and is selecting the target for the bounce effect. Looking more carefully: the opponent cast Jeskai Revelation, and Kimi25 is being asked to select the target for the 'return target spell or permanent to its owner's hand' part. Actually, re-reading: it says 'Select a spell or permanent' and one of the choices IS Jeskai Revelation itself. If Kimi25 bounces Jeskai Revelation back to the opponent's hand, the spell would be returned to hand and the rest of its effects would still resolve (since the spell is already on the stack resolving). So bouncing the spell itself doesn't fizzle it. However, bouncing Steam Vents is still a very low-value choice. Kimi25 could bounce their own Seam Rip to replay it later, or bounce the opponent's land. But the real question is: why didn't Kimi25 counter Jeskai Revelation with No More Lies (costs WU, opponent has 4 untapped lands but needs to pay 3 extra)? The opponent has Steam Vents, Riverpyre Verge, Island, and potentially one more untapped - they have exactly 4 untapped mana sources, so they could pay the 3. Actually looking at the board: Sonnet Vorthos has Steam Vents (untapped), Riverpyre Verge (untapped), Island (untapped) = 3 untapped lands, so they could pay exactly 3. So No More Lies wouldn't work. But bouncing a random land instead of something more impactful is still suboptimal. The real issue is the target choice - bouncing an opponent's untapped Steam Vents is nearly meaningless when they have plenty of other lands. Kimi25 should bounce their own Seam Rip (to replay it as a reusable removal spell) or even Cori Mountain Monastery for value.

Cast Aang's Iceberg when the opponent has zero nonland permanents on the battlefield, making the exile ability completely wasted. Additionally, this tapped out all remaining mana, leaving no ability to hold up any of the three No More Lies or Spell Snare in hand against the opponent's next turn.

Cast Consult the Star Charts without kicker when they had 8 lands available. With the opponent mostly tapped out, they could safely kick it for 4 mana to pick 2 cards from the top 8 instead of just 1, while still holding up 4 mana for No More Lies or other countermagic.

Consult the Star Charts has mana value 2 (its base cost is {1}{U}), making it a legal target for Spell Snare. The opponent is at 9 life with no creatures on board, and Kimi25 has a hand full of reactive cards but no threats. Allowing the opponent to dig through their library for cards (potentially finding threats or answers) is a significant missed opportunity. Spell Snare is a narrow counterspell that may not find a better target, and countering a card advantage spell is one of its best uses.

Opponent cast Consult the Star Charts (mana value 2), which lets them search through 8 cards and pick one. Sonnet Vorthos had 3 Spell Snares in hand and untapped mana (Island, Riverpyre Verge) to cast one, but declined to counter it.

At 9 life facing two 2/2 Monk Tokens (4 damage/turn), Sonnet Vorthos used Burst Lightning to deal 2 to the opponent's face instead of killing a Monk Token. With no creatures on board, a hand full of counterspells that can't remove existing creatures, and only ~2 turns to live against the current board, the 2 face damage is nearly meaningless while removing a token would significantly extend survival time.

Consult the Star Charts (MV 2) is on the stack, and Kimi25 has Spell Snare which perfectly counters MV 2 spells for just {U}. Letting the opponent's card selection/advantage spell resolve for free when holding the ideal counter is a significant missed opportunity. Kimi25 has untapped Hallowed Fountain and Island to cast it.

Consult the Star Charts is a card advantage spell that will let the opponent dig through their library to find threats or answers. With 3 copies of No More Lies in hand and the mana to cast one (Hallowed Fountain and Island are untapped, providing W and U), Kimi25 should counter this spell. Letting the opponent draw cards when you have three counterspells in hand and the mana available is a significant missed opportunity, especially when the opponent is at 9 life and you need to prevent them from finding more threats while you have Day of Judgment as a safety valve.

Declined to counter Consult the Star Charts (MV 2) with Spell Snare when holding 3 copies. Letting the opponent look at top 8 cards and select the best one provides significant card advantage/selection. With 3 Spell Snares in hand, using one here is very reasonable since there's redundancy for future MV 2 threats.

Passed the main phase without casting Stock Up while opponent was completely tapped out. With 3 untapped lands (exactly enough for Stock Up's {2}{U} cost) and the opponent having zero mana available, this was a risk-free window to cast a sorcery. While Kimi25 already has 9 cards in hand (above hand size), the card selection from Stock Up (look at 5, keep 2) would help find win conditions they clearly need, since they appear to have no creatures on board. The reasoning about 'attacking' seems confused since Aang's Iceberg is an enchantment, not a creature.

chosen_display: Aang's Iceberg — waterbend {3}: Sacrifice {this}. If you do, scry ... [Activate]
annotation_description: Sacrificed Aang's Iceberg for scry 2, which returns whatever permanent it was exiling back to the opponent's battlefield, AND taps out all remaining mana so no countermagic (No More Lies x3, Spell Snare) can be held up. The opponent is at 5 life - maintaining control with countermagic is critical. Scry 2 is marginal when the hand already has 7 cards of interaction.
